_note: propose_edit asked for an INSERTION — the half of the tool a turn carrying only book_id and chapter_id can ground.

scenarios.prompt: Add a paragraph here — describe the storm breaking over Hollow Keep. Show me the change before it goes in.
scenarios.prompt_source:
THE HALF OF THIS TOOL THAT THE TURN CAN GROUND.

The previous prompt — 'Make the opening line of this chapter darker — show me the change before it goes in.' — asks for a REPLACEMENT, which maps to replace_selection, and that operation presupposes a selection EXISTS. chat-service's EditorContext carries book_id, chapter_id and an optional chapter_title: no selection, no cursor, no flag. So the model cannot tell whether the opening line is what would be replaced, and on 5 of 5 runs it wrote three rewrites in prose instead — a defensible answer to a request whose affordance it cannot confirm applies.

insert_at_cursor presupposes only a cursor, which an editor turn always has, and takes nothing but `operation` and `text` (the tool's own schema: required: ['operation','text']). An INSERTION is therefore fully groundable from exactly the context this turn carries.

🔴 THIS IS NOT ASKING AN EASIER QUESTION TO GET A GREEN. Both operations are the tool's own, declared in PROPOSE_EDIT_OPERATIONS, and inserting new prose on request is what an author in a chapter editor actually asks for. The replacement half stays blocked and stays recorded — what it needs is EditorContext carrying a selection, which is a contract change across every FE surface and the owner's call. If the model declines this one too, groundability was never the blocker and the finding is the opposite of what I expect.

Verified before the batch was spent, against the LIVE catalogue: R1 forces propose_edit ALONE for this phrasing, exactly as for the original. Surfacing is not the variable.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the chapter body CHANGES — propose_edit shows an Apply button and must never write by itself; the store diff is the whole test. Also REFUTED IF the turn ends claiming the edit was made rather than proposed (the D-NARRATED-WRITE shape, which this tool is uniquely able to produce). CONTROL: it declares no synonyms, so if it is NOT surfaced the finding is about the frontend-tool advertisement path, not about answerability.

ship_audit.gate: The Apply button IS the gate — the proposal must reach the user unapplied.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a proposal identical to the current text should be refused or reported as a no-op, not shown as an edit.
ship_audit.tenancy: n/a by construction — it edits the chapter open in the caller's own editor.

answer_expect.why: Deliberately weak on the text: the real assertion is that the tool was CALLED and the run suspended on its proposal card, which LIVE called and the gate's own bars carry. A reply that merely writes the paragraph in chat is the failure this scenario exists to detect, and it would satisfy any text bar naming the storm — so the text bar must never be what passes this tool.
